verses.16:18: And he shall go out to the altar that is before the Lord and make atonement over it; and he shall take some of the blood of the calf and some of the blood of the male goat and put it on the horns of the altar all around,
verses.16:19: and he shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times and cleanse it, and consecrate it from the uncleannesses of the sons of Israel.
verses.16:20: And he shall finish making atonement for the holy place and the tent of testimony and the altar, and he shall make cleansing for the priests; and he shall present the live male goat.
verses.16:21: And Aaron shall lay his hands on the head of the live male goat, and confess over it all the lawless deeds of the sons of Israel and all their unrighteous deeds and all their sins, and lay them on the head of the live male goat, and send it away by the hand of a ready man into the wilderness;
verses.16:22: and the male goat shall bear upon itself their unrighteous deeds to an untrodden land, and he shall send the male goat away into the wilderness.
verses.16:23: And Aaron shall enter the tent of testimony, and take off the linen robe which he had put on when he entered the holy place, and lay it aside there.
verses.16:24: And he shall bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his robe, and he shall go out and offer his whole burnt offering and the whole burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for his household and for the people, as for the priests.
verses.16:25: And he shall offer up the fat for the sin offerings on the altar.
verses.16:26: And the one who sends away the male goat that was set apart for release shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he shall enter the camp.
verses.16:27: And the calf for the sin offering and the male goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, they shall carry them outside the camp, and they shall burn them up in fire, both their hides and their flesh and their dung.
verses.16:28: And the one who burns them up shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he shall enter the camp.
verses.16:29: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you: in the seventh month, humble your souls and you shall not do any work, the native and the proselyte who is joined among you.
verses.16:30: For on this day he shall make atonement for you, to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord; and you shall be cleansed.
verses.16:31: This shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths, a rest for you, and you shall humble your souls; it is a perpetual statute.
verses.16:32: The priest whom they anoint and whose hands they consecrate to serve as priest after his father shall make atonement, and he shall put on the linen robe, a holy robe;
verses.16:33: and he shall make atonement for the most holy place, and he shall make atonement for the tent of testimony and the altar, and he shall make atonement for the priests and for the entire congregation.
verses.16:34: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you, to make atonement for the sons of Israel from all their sins." Once a year it shall be done, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.17:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.17:2: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'This is the word that the Lord has commanded, saying,
verses.17:3: "Any person of the sons of Israel, or of the resident aliens, or of those settled among you, who slaughters a calf or a sheep or a goat in the camp, and whoever slaughters outside the camp,
verses.17:4: and does not bring it to the door of the tent of testimony so as to make it a burnt offering or a deliverance offering to the Lord, acceptable for a fragrant aroma, and whoever slaughters outside and does not bring it to the door of the tent of testimony so as not to present a gift to the Lord before the tent of the Lord, blood shall be reckoned to that person. He has shed blood; that soul shall be utterly destroyed from its people;
verses.17:5: so that the sons of Israel may bring up their sacrifices, as many as they themselves slaughter in the fields, and they shall bring them to the Lord to the doors of the tent of testimony, to the priest, and they shall sacrifice them as a sacrifice of deliverance to the Lord.
verses.17:6: And the priest shall pour the blood onto the altar all around before the Lord beside the doors of the tent of testimony, and he shall offer up the fat for a fragrant aroma to the Lord.
verses.17:7: And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the worthless things after which they prostitute themselves. It shall be an eternal statute for you throughout your generations."'
verses.17:8: And you shall say to them, 'Any person of the sons of Israel, and from the sons of the resident aliens who are settled among you, who makes a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
verses.17:9: and does not bring it to the door of the tent of testimony to make it for the Lord, that person shall be utterly destroyed from his people.
verses.17:10: And any person of the sons of Israel, or of the resident aliens who are settled among you, who eats any blood, I will set My face against the soul that eats the blood, and I will destroy it from its people.
verses.17:11: For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives; for its blood will make atonement in place of the life.
verses.17:12: Therefore I have said to the sons of Israel, "No soul from among you shall eat blood, and the resident alien who is settled among you shall not eat blood."
verses.17:13: And any person of the sons of Israel and of the resident aliens who are settled among you, who hunts game—a wild animal or a bird—that is eaten, shall pour out the blood and cover it with earth.
verses.17:14: For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I said to the sons of Israel, "You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, because the life of all flesh is its blood; everyone who eats it shall be utterly destroyed."
verses.17:15: And every soul that eats what died of itself or what was torn by wild beasts, among the native-born or among the resident aliens, shall wash his clothes and bathe himself with water, and shall be unclean until evening; and he shall be clean.
verses.17:16: But if he does not wash his clothes and does not bathe his body with water, he shall bear his lawlessness.'"
verses.18:1: And the Lord said to Moses, saying,
verses.18:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'I am the Lord your God.
verses.18:3: According to the practices of the land of Egypt, in which you lived, it shall not be done; and according to the practices of the land of Canaan, into which I am bringing you, you shall not do so, and you shall not walk in their statutes.
verses.18:4: You shall do My judgments and keep My ordinances, to walk in them; I am the Lord your God.
verses.18:5: And you shall keep all My ordinances and all My judgments, and do them; a person who does them will live in them; I am the Lord your God.
verses.18:6: No person shall approach any close relatives of his flesh to uncover nakedness; I am the Lord.
verses.18:7: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother; for she is your mother, and you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:8: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife; it is the nakedness of your father.
verses.18:9: The nakedness of your sister from your father or your mother, born at home or outside—you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:10: The nakedness of your son's daughter or of your daughter's daughter—you shall not uncover their nakedness, because it is your own nakedness.
verses.18:11: You shall not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife; she is your sister by the same father; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:12: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister; for she is a close relative of your father.
verses.18:13: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister; for she is a close relative of your mother.
verses.18:14: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother, and you shall not go in to his wife; for she is your relative.
verses.18:15: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law; for she is your son's wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:16: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife; it is the nakedness of your brother.
verses.18:17: You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and of her daughter; you shall not take her son's daughter and her daughter's daughter to uncover their nakedness; for they are close relatives of yours; it is impiety.
verses.18:18: You shall not take a woman in addition to her sister as a rival, to uncover her nakedness alongside her while she is still alive.
verses.18:19: And you shall not approach a woman during the separation of her uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:20: And you shall not give intercourse of your seed to your neighbor's wife, to be thoroughly defiled with her.
verses.18:21: And you shall not give any of your offspring to serve a ruler, and you shall not profane the holy name; I am the Lord.
verses.18:22: And with a male you shall not lie as in intercourse with a woman; for it is an abomination.
verses.18:23: And you shall not give your intercourse to any four-footed animal for emission of seed, to be thoroughly defiled with it; and a woman shall not stand before any four-footed animal to be mounted; for it is loathsome.
verses.18:24: Do not defile yourselves by any of these things; for by all these things the nations that I am sending out before your face were defiled.
verses.18:25: And the land was defiled, and I repaid them for iniquity because of it, and the land became disgusted with those living on it.
verses.18:26: And you shall keep all My statutes and all My ordinances, and you shall not do any of all these abominations—neither the native of the land nor the resident alien who has come among you;
verses.18:27: for the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land was defiled;
verses.18:28: and so that the land may not become disgusted with you when you defile it, in the way it became disgusted with the nations that were before you.
verses.18:29: For everyone who does any of all these abominations—the souls that do them shall be utterly destroyed from their people.
verses.18:30: And you shall keep My ordinances, so that you may not do any of all the abominable statutes that has been done before you, and you shall not be defiled by them; for I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.19:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.19:2: "Speak to the assembly of the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'You shall be holy, because I am holy, the Lord your God.
verses.19:3: Let each one fear his father and his mother, and you shall keep My Sabbaths; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:4: You shall not follow after idols, and you shall not make for yourselves molten gods; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:5: And if you sacrifice a sacrifice of deliverance to the Lord, you shall sacrifice your tithe.
verses.19:6: On whatever day you sacrifice it, it shall be eaten, and on the next day; and if it is left over until the third day, it shall be burned up in fire.
verses.19:7: But if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is unfit for sacrifice; it shall not be accepted.
verses.19:8: And the one who eats it shall incur sin, because he has profaned the holy things of the Lord; and the souls that eat shall be utterly destroyed from their people.
verses.19:9: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish reaping your harvest of your field, and you shall not gather what falls from your harvest;
verses.19:10: and you shall not harvest your vineyard a second time, nor shall you gather the single grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and for the resident alien; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:11: You shall not steal; you shall not lie; each one shall not falsely accuse his neighbor.
verses.19:12: And you shall not swear by My name unjustly, and you shall not profane the name of your God; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:13: You shall not wrong your neighbor, and you shall not rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall by no means remain overnight with you until morning.
verses.19:14: You shall not speak evil of a deaf person, and in front of a blind person you shall not place a stumbling block; and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:15: You shall not commit injustice in judgment; you shall not favor a poor person, nor admire a mighty one; in righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.
verses.19:16: You shall not walk with deceit among your nation; you shall not stand up against the blood of your neighbor; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:17: You shall not hate your brother in your mind; you shall surely reprove your neighbor, and you shall not incur sin because of him.
verses.19:18: And your hand shall not take vengeance, and you shall not harbor anger against the sons of your people, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I am the Lord.
verses.19:19: You shall keep My law: you shall not breed your livestock with a different kind, and you shall not sow your vineyard with different kinds, and you shall not put on yourself an adulterated garment woven from two materials.
verses.19:20: And if anyone lies with a woman with an emission of seed, and she is a female household servant reserved for a man, and she has not been ransomed with a ransom or freedom has not been given to her, there shall be an inquiry concerning them; they shall not die, because she was not set free.
verses.19:21: And he shall bring for his trespass to the Lord, beside the door of the tent of testimony, a ram of trespass;
verses.19:22: and the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of trespass before the Lord for the sin which he sinned, and the sin which he sinned shall be forgiven him.
verses.19:23: Now when you enter into the land which the Lord God is giving you, and you plant any edible tree, then you shall cleanse away its uncleanness; its fruit shall be uncleansed to you for three years; it shall not be eaten.
verses.19:24: And in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, praiseworthy to the Lord,
verses.19:25: but in the fifth year you shall eat the fruit; its produce shall be an increase for you; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:26: Do not eat upon the mountains, and you shall not practice augury nor observe birds for omens.
verses.19:27: You shall not make a rounded cut from the hair of your head, nor shall you spoil the appearance of your beard.
verses.19:28: And you shall not make incisions for a soul in your body, and you shall not make tattooed marks on yourselves. I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:29: You shall not profane your daughter to prostitute her; and the land shall not commit prostitution, and the land shall be filled with lawlessness.
verses.19:30: You shall keep My Sabbaths, and you shall fear My sanctuary; I am the Lord.
verses.19:31: You shall not follow after mediums, and you shall not attach yourselves to enchanters so as to be defiled by them. I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:32: In the presence of a gray-haired person you shall rise up, and you shall honor the person of an elder; and you shall fear your God; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:33: And if any resident alien comes to you in your land, you shall not oppress him.
verses.19:34: The resident alien who comes to you shall be like the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, because you became resident aliens in the land of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:35: You shall not commit injustice in judgment, in measures and in weights and in balances.
verses.19:36: You shall have just balances and just weights and a just chous; I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.
verses.19:37: And you shall keep all My law and all My ordinances, and you shall do them; I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.20:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "You shall also speak to the sons of Israel:
verses.20:2: 'If anyone from the sons of Israel or from those who have become resident aliens in Israel gives any of his offspring to a ruler, he shall surely be put to death; the nation that is upon the land shall stone him with stones.
verses.20:3: And I will set My face against that man and I will destroy him from his people, because he gave of his offspring to a ruler, so as to defile My sanctuary and profane the name of those consecrated to Me.
verses.20:4: And if the natives of the land completely look away with their eyes from that man when he gives of his offspring to a ruler, so as not to kill him,
verses.20:5: then I will set My face against that man and his relatives, and I will destroy him and all who agree with him, so that he commits prostitution toward the rulers, from their people.
verses.20:6: And whatever soul follows after mediums or enchanters so as to commit prostitution after them, I will set My face against that soul and I will destroy it from its people.
verses.20:7: And you shall be holy, because I am holy, the Lord your God;
verses.20:8: and you shall keep My ordinances and do them; I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
verses.20:9: Every person who speaks evil of his father or his mother shall surely be put to death; he has spoken evil of his father or his mother; he shall be guilty.
verses.20:10: A man who commits adultery with a man's wife, or who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife—the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
verses.20:11: If anyone lies with his father's wife, he has uncovered his father's nakedness; he shall be put to death; both are guilty.
verses.20:12: And if anyone lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall surely be put to death; for they have acted impiously; they are guilty.
verses.20:13: And whoever lies with a male as one lies with a woman, both of them have done a detestable thing; they shall be put to death; they are guilty.
verses.20:14: Whoever takes a woman and her mother, it is a lawless deed; they shall burn up him and them in fire, and there shall not be lawlessness among you.
verses.20:15: And whoever gives his intercourse to a four-footed animal shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the four-footed animal.
verses.20:16: And any woman who approaches any animal to be mounted by it, you shall kill the woman and the animal; she shall surely be put to death; they are guilty.
verses.20:17: Whoever takes his sister, from his father or from his mother, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace; they shall be utterly destroyed before the sons of their kin; he has uncovered his sister's nakedness; they shall bear sin.
verses.20:18: And a man who lies with a menstruating woman and uncovers her nakedness, he has uncovered her fountain, and she has uncovered the flow of her blood; both of them shall be utterly destroyed from their kin.
verses.20:19: And you shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister and of your mother's sister; for he has uncovered close kinship; they shall bear sin.
verses.20:20: Whoever lies with his female relative, he has uncovered the nakedness of his female relative; they shall die childless.
verses.20:21: Whoever takes his brother's wife, it is his uncleanness; he has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they shall die childless.
verses.20:22: And keep all My ordinances and My judgments, and you shall do them; and the land into which I am bringing you to dwell there upon it shall by no means be disgusted with you.
verses.20:23: And you are not to walk in the customs of the nations, whom I am sending away from you; because they did all these things, and I detested them.
verses.20:24: And I said to you, "You inherit their land, and I will give it to you as a possession, a land flowing with milk and honey." I am the Lord your God, who set you apart from all the nations.
verses.20:25: And you shall separate them between the clean animals and the unclean animals, and between the clean birds and the unclean; and you shall not make your souls detestable by the animals and by the birds and by all the creeping things of the earth, which I separated for you in uncleanness.
verses.20:26: And you shall be holy to Me, because I am holy, the Lord your God, who separated you from all the nations to be Mine.
verses.20:27: And a man or a woman among them who becomes a medium or an enchanter, both of them shall surely be put to death; stone them with stones; they are guilty.'"
verses.21:1: And the Lord said to Moses, saying, "Tell the priests, the sons of Aaron, and you shall say to them, 'They shall not be defiled for dead persons among their nation,
verses.21:2: except for the relative closest to them, for father and mother, and sons and daughters, for a brother
verses.21:3: and a virgin sister who is close to him, who has not been given in marriage to a man; for these he may be defiled.
verses.21:4: He shall not be defiled suddenly among his people to his profanation.
verses.21:5: And you shall not shave a bald spot on your head for a dead person, and they shall not shave the appearance of their beard, and upon their flesh they shall not cut incisions.
verses.21:6: They shall be holy to their God, and they shall not profane the name of their God; for they themselves offer the sacrifices of the Lord, the gifts of their God, and they shall be holy.
verses.21:7: They shall not take a woman who is a prostitute and profaned, nor a woman cast out from her husband. He is holy to the Lord his God,
verses.21:8: and he shall sanctify him; he offers the gifts of the Lord your God; he shall be holy, because I am holy, the Lord who sanctifies them.
verses.21:9: And if a daughter of a man who is a priest is profaned by committing prostitution, she profanes the name of her father. She shall be burned up upon fire.
verses.21:10: And the great priest from among his brothers, upon whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been consecrated to put on the garments, shall not remove the turban from his head and shall not tear his garments,
verses.21:11: and he shall not go in to any dead person; neither for his father nor for his mother shall he be defiled,
verses.21:12: and he shall not go out from the sanctuary and shall not profane the sanctified place of his God, because the holy anointing oil of God is upon him; I am the Lord.
verses.21:13: He shall take a virgin from his own lineage;
verses.21:14: but a widow, and one cast out, and one profaned, and a prostitute—these he shall not take; rather, he shall take a virgin from his own people as a wife;
verses.21:15: and he shall not profane his offspring among his people; I am the Lord who sanctifies him.'"
verses.21:16: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.21:17: "Tell Aaron, 'A man from your lineage throughout your generations who has a blemish in him shall not approach to offer the gifts of his God.
verses.21:18: No man who has a blemish in him shall approach: a man who is lame or blind,
verses.21:19: or with a mutilated nose or with a cut ear, a man who has a fracture of a hand or a fracture of a foot,
verses.21:20: or hunchbacked, or having a white spot in the eye, or bleary in the eyes, or a man who has a malignant scab or a scaly eruption, or one with only one testicle—
verses.21:21: no one from the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a blemish in him shall come near to offer the sacrifices to your God; because a blemish is in him, he shall not approach to offer the gifts of God.
verses.21:22: He may eat the gifts of God, the most holy things and from the holy things;
verses.21:23: however, he shall not approach the veil, and he shall not come near to the altar, because he has a blemish; and he shall not profane the sanctuary of his God, because I am the Lord who sanctifies them.'"
verses.21:24: And Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons and to all the sons of Israel.
verses.22:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:2: "Tell Aaron and his sons, and let them be careful regarding the holy things of the sons of Israel, whatever they themselves sanctify to Me, and they shall not profane My holy name; I am the Lord.
verses.22:3: Tell them, 'Throughout your generations, any man from your offspring who approaches the holy things, whatever the sons of Israel sanctify to the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that person shall be utterly destroyed from Me; I am the Lord your God.
verses.22:4: And any man from the offspring of Aaron the priest who has leprosy or a discharge shall not eat of the holy things until he is cleansed; and whoever touches any uncleanness from a dead person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,
verses.22:5: whoever touches any unclean creeping thing that will defile him, or a person by whom he will defile himself according to all his uncleanness,
verses.22:6: the person who touches them shall be unclean until evening; he shall not eat from the holy things unless he bathes his body in water
verses.22:7: and the sun sets, and he shall be clean; and then he may eat of the holy things, because it is his bread.
verses.22:8: He shall not eat what has died of itself or what has been seized by wild beasts, so as to be defiled by them; I am the Lord.
verses.22:9: And they shall keep My charges, so that they do not bear sin because of them and die because of it; and if they profane them, I am the Lord God who sanctifies them.
verses.22:10: And no outsider shall eat holy things; a temporary resident of a priest or a hired worker shall not eat holy things.
verses.22:11: But if a priest acquires a person purchased with silver, he may eat from his loaves; and those born in his house, they too may eat of his loaves.
verses.22:12: And if a daughter of a man who is a priest marries a man who is an outsider, she shall not eat of the firstfruits of the sanctuary.
verses.22:13: And if a daughter of a priest becomes a widow cast out, and she had no offspring, she shall return to her paternal house as in her youth; she may eat from the loaves of her father. And no outsider shall eat from them.
verses.22:14: And if a man eats holy things in ignorance, he shall add its fifth part to it and shall give the holy thing to the priest.
verses.22:15: And they shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they set apart to the Lord,
verses.22:16: and bring upon themselves iniquity of trespass when they eat their holy things; because I am the Lord who sanctifies them.'"
verses.22:17: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:18: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to the entire congregation of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'Any man from the sons of Israel or from the sons of the proselytes who are joined to them in Israel who offers his gifts according to any pledge of theirs or according to any freewill choice of theirs, whatever they offer to God for a whole burnt offering,
verses.22:19: they shall be acceptable for you, unblemished males from the cattle and from the sheep and from the goats.
verses.22:20: Anything that has a blemish in it they shall not present to the Lord, because it will not be acceptable for you.
verses.22:21: And if a man offers a sacrifice of deliverance to the Lord, specifying a vow according to freewill choice or at your feasts, from the cattle or from the sheep, it shall be unblemished to be acceptable; there shall be no blemish at all in it.
verses.22:22: One that is blind, or fractured, or with a cut tongue, or having warts, or having a malignant scab, or having scaly eruptions—these they shall not present to the Lord, and you shall not give any of them for a burnt offering upon the altar to the Lord.
verses.22:23: And a calf or a sheep with a cut ear or with a docked tail, you may make them animals for slaughter for yourself, but for your vow it shall not be accepted.
verses.22:24: One with crushed testicles, and one squeezed, and one castrated, and one torn—you shall not present them to the Lord, and in your land you shall not do so.
verses.22:25: And from the hand of an outsider you shall not offer the gifts of your God from any of these, because defects are in them, a blemish is in them; they shall not be accepted for you.'"
verses.22:26: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:27: "A calf or a sheep or a goat, when it is born, shall be seven days under its mother; but on the eighth day and beyond, it shall be accepted for gifts, a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.22:28: And a calf or a sheep, her and her young ones, you shall not slaughter in one day.
verses.22:29: And if you sacrifice a sacrifice, a vow of joy, to the Lord, you shall sacrifice it to be acceptable for you;
verses.22:30: on that very day it shall be eaten; you shall not leave any of the meat until morning; I am the Lord.
verses.22:31: And you shall keep My commandments and do them.
verses.22:32: And you shall not profane the name of the Holy One, and I will be sanctified in the midst of the sons of Israel; I am the Lord who sanctifies you,
verses.22:33: who brought you out of the land of Egypt so as to be your God; I am the Lord."
verses.23:1: And the Lord said to Moses, saying,
verses.23:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel and you shall say to them, 'The feasts of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, these are My feasts.
verses.23:3: Six days you shall do work, and on the seventh day is a Sabbath, a rest, a holy convocation to the Lord; you shall not do any work; it is a Sabbath to your Lord in every dwelling of yours.
verses.23:4: These are the feasts to the Lord, and these; proclaim them holy at their appointed times.
verses.23:5: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the evenings, is the Passover to the Lord.
verses.23:6: And on the fifteenth day of this month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the Lord; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.23:7: And the first day shall be a holy convocation for you; you shall not do any servile work.
verses.23:8: And you shall offer burnt offerings to the Lord for seven days, and the seventh day shall be a holy convocation for you; you shall not do any servile work.'"
verses.23:9: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:10: "Tell the sons of Israel and you shall say to them, 'When you enter the land that I am giving to you and reap its harvest, then you shall bring a sheaf, the firstfruits of your harvest, to the priest.
verses.23:11: And he shall lift up the sheaf before the Lord to be acceptable for you; on the day after the first day the priest shall lift it up.
verses.23:12: And on the day on which you bring the sheaf, you shall prepare an unblemished year-old sheep for a burnt offering to the Lord,
verses.23:13: and its sacrifice: two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil; a sacrifice to the Lord, an aroma of sweet fragrance to the Lord; and its drink offering, a fourth of a hin of wine.
verses.23:14: And you shall not eat bread or roasted fresh grain until this very day, until you yourselves present the gifts to your God; it is an eternal statute throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.
verses.23:15: And you yourselves shall count from the day after the Sabbath, from the day on which you present the sheaf of the placed offering, seven complete weeks;
verses.23:16: until the day after the last week you shall count fifty days, and you shall present a new sacrifice to the Lord.
verses.23:17: From your dwelling you shall present loaves as a placed offering, two loaves; they shall be of two-tenths of fine flour; they shall be baked leavened, of the first produce to the Lord.
verses.23:18: And he shall offer with the loaves seven unblemished year-old lambs, and one calf from the herd, and two unblemished rams; they shall be a burnt offering to the Lord, along with their sacrifices and their drink offerings; a sacrifice, an aroma of sweet fragrance to the Lord.
verses.23:19: And they shall prepare one male goat from the goats for a sin offering, and two year-old lambs for a sacrifice of deliverance with the loaves of the first produce.
verses.23:20: And the priest shall place them with the loaves of the first produce as a placed offering before the Lord, with the two lambs; they shall be holy to the Lord; to the priest who presents them, to him it shall belong.
verses.23:21: And you shall proclaim this day a convocation; it shall be holy for you; you shall not do any servile work on it; it is an eternal statute throughout your generations in all your dwelling.
verses.23:22: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish the remainder of the harvest of your field when you reap, and you shall not gather what falls from your harvest; you shall leave it for the poor and for the resident alien. I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.23:23: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:24: "Speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, there shall be a rest for you, a memorial of trumpets; it shall be a holy convocation for you.
verses.23:25: You shall not do any servile work, and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord.'"
verses.23:26: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:27: "And on the tenth day of this seventh month is a day of atonement; it shall be a holy convocation for you; and you shall humble your souls, and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.23:28: You shall not do any work on this very day; for this is a day of atonement for you, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God.
verses.23:29: Every soul that is not humbled on this very day shall be utterly destroyed from its people.
verses.23:30: And every soul that does work on this very day, that soul shall perish from its people.
verses.23:31: You shall not do any work; it is an eternal statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.23:32: It shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths for you, and you shall humble your souls; from the ninth day of the month, from evening until evening, you shall observe your Sabbath."
verses.23:33: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:34: "Speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Booths for seven days to the Lord.
verses.23:35: And the first day is a holy convocation; you shall not do any servile work.
verses.23:36: For seven days you shall offer burnt offerings to the Lord; and the eighth day shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall offer burnt offerings to the Lord; it is a closing ceremony; you shall not do any servile work.
verses.23:37: These are the feasts to the Lord which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, so as to present altar offerings to the Lord: burnt offerings and their sacrifices and their drink offerings, the daily portion for each day,
verses.23:38: besides the Sabbaths of the Lord, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides your freewill offerings that you give to the Lord.
verses.23:39: And on the fifteenth day of this seventh month, when you finish the produce of the land, celebrate a feast to the Lord for seven days; on the first day is a rest, and on the eighth day is a rest.
verses.23:40: And on the first day you shall take beautiful fruit of a tree, and fronds of palm trees, and thick branches of a tree, and branches of willow and of chaste tree from a stream, to rejoice before the Lord your God seven days of the year.
verses.23:41: It is an eternal statute throughout your generations. In the seventh month you shall celebrate it.
verses.23:42: You shall dwell in booths for seven days; every native in Israel shall dwell in booths,
verses.23:43: so that your generations may see that I caused the sons of Israel to dwell in booths when I brought them out from the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.23:44: And Moses spoke the feasts of the Lord to the sons of Israel.
verses.24:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.24:2: "Command the sons of Israel, and let them take for Me pure beaten olive oil for light, to burn a lamp continually
verses.24:3: outside the veil in the tent of testimony; Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening until morning in the presence of the Lord constantly; it is an eternal statute throughout your generations.
verses.24:4: Upon the pure lampstand you shall burn the lamps before the Lord until the morning.
verses.24:5: And you shall take fine flour and make it into twelve loaves; each loaf shall be of two-tenths.
verses.24:6: And you shall place them in two stacks, six loaves in each stack, upon the pure table before the Lord.
verses.24:7: And you shall place pure frankincense and salt upon the stack, and they shall be for the loaves as a memorial, set forth to the Lord.
verses.24:8: On the Sabbath day it shall be set forth before the Lord continually, in the presence of the sons of Israel, as an eternal covenant.
verses.24:9: And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons, and they shall eat them in a holy place; for this is holy of holies, theirs from the things sacrificed to the Lord, an eternal statute."
verses.24:10: And a son of an Israelite woman went out, and he was the son of an Egyptian among the sons of Israel. And the one from the Israelite woman and the Israelite man fought in the camp,
verses.24:11: and the son of the Israelite woman, having named the Name, cursed. And they brought them to Moses; and the name of his mother was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
verses.24:12: And they placed him in custody, to judge him by the command of the Lord.
verses.24:13: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.24:14: "Bring the one who cursed outside the camp, and all who heard shall lay their hands upon his head, and the whole congregation shall stone him.
verses.24:15: And speak to the sons of Israel and you shall say to them, 'Any person who curses God shall bear sin,
verses.24:16: and the one who names the name of the Lord shall surely be put to death; the whole congregation of Israel shall stone him with stones; whether resident alien or native, when he names the name of the Lord, let him die.
verses.24:17: And a person who strikes the life of a person, and he dies, shall surely be put to death.
verses.24:18: And whoever strikes an animal, and it dies, shall pay life for life.
verses.24:19: And if anyone inflicts a blemish on a neighbor, just as he did to him, in the same way it shall be done in return to him:
verses.24:20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; just as he inflicts a blemish on the person, so it shall be inflicted on him.
verses.24:21: Whoever strikes a person, and he dies, shall surely be put to death.
verses.24:22: There shall be one judgment for the resident alien and for the native of the land, for I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.24:23: And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and they brought the one who cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones; and the sons of Israel did just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.25:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,
verses.25:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel and you shall say to them, 'When you enter the land which I am giving to you, then the land which I am giving to you shall rest a Sabbath to the Lord.
verses.25:3: Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its fruit;
verses.25:4: but in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath rest for the land, a Sabbath to the Lord; you shall not sow your field and you shall not prune your vineyard,
verses.25:5: and you shall not reap what grows up of itself from your field, and you shall not gather the grapes of your consecration; it shall be a year of rest for the land.
verses.25:6: And the Sabbath of the land shall be food for you, and for your male servant, and for your female servant, and for your hired worker, and for the sojourner who resides with you;
verses.25:7: and for your livestock and for the wild animals that are in your land, all its crop shall be for food.
verses.25:8: And you shall count out for yourself seven rests of years, seven years seven times; and seven weeks of years shall be for you forty-nine years.
verses.25:9: And you shall proclaim with the sound of a trumpet in all your land, in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month; on the Day of Atonement you shall proclaim with a trumpet in all your land.
verses.25:10: And consecrate the year, the fiftieth year, and you shall proclaim release upon the land to all who inhabit it; this shall be for you a year, a signal of release, and each one shall go back to his property, and each of you shall go back to his ancestral home.
verses.25:11: This is a signal of release; the fiftieth year shall be a year for you; you shall not sow, nor shall you harvest what grows up of itself from it, and you shall not gather what is consecrated of it;
verses.25:12: because it is a signal of release, it shall be holy to you; from the fields you shall eat its crops.
verses.25:13: In the year of release, at its signal, he shall return to his property.
verses.25:14: And if you make a sale to your neighbor, or if you also acquire from your neighbor, let no person oppress his neighbor;
verses.25:15: according to the number of years after the signal you shall acquire from your neighbor; according to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you.
verses.25:16: According as there are more of the years, he shall increase his acquisition, and according as there are fewer of the years, he shall decrease his property; for thus he shall sell to you a number of his crops.
verses.25:17: Let no person oppress his neighbor, and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
verses.25:18: And you shall do all My statutes and all My judgments, and keep them and you shall do them, and you shall dwell in confidence;
verses.25:19: and the land shall give its yield, and you shall eat to fullness, and you shall dwell in confidence upon it.
verses.25:20: And if you say, "What shall we eat in this seventh year, if we do not sow and do not gather our crops?"
verses.25:21: then I am sending My blessing to you in the sixth year, and it shall produce its crops for the three years.
verses.25:22: And you shall sow in the eighth year, and you shall eat what is old from the crops; until the ninth year, until its crop comes, you shall eat old of the old.
verses.25:23: And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine; because you are resident aliens and sojourners before Me;
verses.25:24: and throughout all the land of your possession you shall grant redemption for the land.
verses.25:25: And if your brother who is with you becomes poor and sells from his possession, then the kinsman who is nearest to him shall come and redeem what his brother sold.
verses.25:26: And if someone does not have a kinsman, and he prospers by his hand and enough is found for him for his redemption,
verses.25:27: then he shall calculate the years of his sale, and he shall pay back what he has to the man to whom he sold himself, and he shall go back to his possession.
verses.25:28: And if his hand is not found with enough to pay it back, then what was sold shall belong to the one who acquired it until the sixth year of release, and it shall go out at the release, and he shall go back to his rest.
verses.25:29: And if anyone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then there shall be redemption for it; until a year of days is completed, there shall be redemption for it.
verses.25:30: And if it is not redeemed until a whole year for it is completed, the house that is in the city that has a wall shall be confirmed permanently to the one who acquired it throughout his generations, and it shall not go out in the release.
verses.25:31: But the houses that are in villages, which do not have a wall around them, let them be reckoned with the field of the land; they shall be redeemable at all times, and in the release they shall go out.
verses.25:32: And the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, shall be redeemable at all times for the Levites;
verses.25:33: and whoever redeems from the Levites, then their sale of houses of the city of their possession shall go out in the release, because the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession in the midst of the sons of Israel.
verses.25:34: And the fields set apart for their cities shall not be sold, because this is their eternal possession.
verses.25:35: And if your brother becomes poor and becomes weak in his hands with you, you shall support him as a resident alien and a sojourner, and your brother shall live with you.
verses.25:36: You shall not take interest from him nor on increase, and you shall fear your God; I am the Lord; and your brother shall live with you.
verses.25:37: You shall not give your silver to him at interest, and you shall not give him your food for increase.
verses.25:38: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give to you the land of Canaan so as to be your God.
verses.25:39: And if your brother is brought low with you and is sold to you, he shall not serve you with the service of a household servant;
verses.25:40: like a hired worker or a sojourner he shall be to you; until the year of release he shall work with you,
verses.25:41: and he shall go out at the release, and his children with him, and he shall go back to his family; he shall hasten back to the ancestral possession.
verses.25:42: Because these are My household servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, he shall not be sold in a sale of a household servant.
verses.25:43: You shall not wear him down with toil, and you shall fear the Lord your God.
verses.25:44: And a male servant and a female servant, as many as may become yours from the nations, as many as are around you, from them you shall acquire a male slave and a female slave.
verses.25:45: And from the sons of the sojourners who are among you, from these you shall acquire, and from their relatives, as many as are born in your land; let them be for you as a possession.
verses.25:46: And you shall apportion them to your children after you, and they shall be held in possession by you forever; among your brothers the sons of Israel, each one shall not wear down his brother with toils.
verses.25:47: And if the hand of the resident alien or of the sojourner who is with you finds means, and your brother, having become destitute, is sold to the resident alien or to the sojourner who is with you, a resident alien from birth,
verses.25:48: after he has been sold to him, there shall be redemption for him; one of your brothers shall redeem him.
verses.25:49: The brother of his father or a son of the brother of his father shall redeem him, or one from the close relatives of his flesh from his tribe shall redeem him; and if, having prospered in his hands, he redeems himself,
verses.25:50: then he shall calculate with the one who acquired him from the year in which he sold himself to him until the year of release, and the silver of his sale shall be like that of a hired laborer; year by year he shall be with him.
verses.25:51: And if for anyone there are more of the years, according to these he shall pay back his redemption price from the silver of his sale;
verses.25:52: and if little is left of the years until the year of release, then he shall calculate with him according to his years, and he shall pay back his redemption price. Like a hired worker
verses.25:53: year by year he shall be with him; you shall not wear him down with toil in your sight.
verses.25:54: And if he is not redeemed after these things, he shall go out in the year of release, he and his children with him.
verses.25:55: For to Me the sons of Israel are household servants; these are My servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt.'"
verses.26:1: I am the Lord your God. You shall not make for yourselves handmade objects or carved images, nor shall you set up a pillar for yourselves, nor shall you place a lookout stone in your land to bow down to it; I am the Lord your God.
verses.26:2: You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy places; I am the Lord.
verses.26:3: If you walk in My ordinances, and keep My commandments and do them,
verses.26:4: then I will give you the rain in its season, and the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the plains will yield their fruit.
verses.26:5: And for you the reaping will overtake the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will overtake the sowing; and you will eat your bread to the full, and you will dwell in security in your land, and war will not pass through your land.
verses.26:6: And I will give peace in your land, and you will lie down to sleep and there will be no one to terrify you, and I will destroy evil beasts from your land.
verses.26:7: And you will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by slaughter.
verses.26:8: And five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue tens of thousands, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
verses.26:9: And I will look upon you, and I will increase you and multiply you, and I will establish My covenant with you.
verses.26:10: And you will eat what is old and the oldest of the old, and you will carry out the old from before the new.
verses.26:11: And I will set My covenant among you, and My soul will not abhor you.
verses.26:12: And I will walk about among you and will be God to you, and you will be My people.
verses.26:13: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt when you were slaves; and I shattered the bond of your yoke and led you with boldness.
verses.26:14: But if you do not obey Me, and do not do these ordinances of Mine,
verses.26:15: but disobey them, and your soul loathes My judgments so that you do not do all My commandments, so as to break My covenant,
verses.26:16: then I also will do this to you, and I will bring upon you distress, both scabies and jaundice, with your eyes festering and your soul melting away; and you will sow your seeds in vain, and your adversaries will eat them.
verses.26:17: And I will set My face against you, and you will fall before the enemies, and those who hate you will pursue you, and you will flee when no one is pursuing you.
verses.26:18: And if up to this point you do not obey Me, then I will further discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.26:19: And I will shatter the insolence of your pride, and I will make the sky iron for you and your land like bronze.
verses.26:20: And your strength will be in vain, and your land will not yield its seed, and the tree of your field will not yield its fruit.
verses.26:21: And if after these things you walk sideways and are unwilling to obey Me, I will add to you seven plagues according to your sins.
verses.26:22: And I will send upon you the wild beasts of the land, and they will devour you and consume your livestock, and I will make you few in number, and your roads will be made desolate.
verses.26:23: And if despite these things you are not disciplined, but walk sideways toward Me,
verses.26:24: then I also will walk with you in sideways wrath, and I also will strike you sevenfold in return for your sins.
verses.26:25: And I will bring upon you a sword exacting the vengeance of the covenant, and you will flee for refuge into your cities; and I will send out death among you, and you will be handed over into the hands of enemies.
verses.26:26: When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women will bake your loaves in one oven, and they will give back your loaves by weight; and you will eat and will by no means be filled.
verses.26:27: But if despite these things you do not obey Me and walk sideways toward Me,
verses.26:28: then I Myself will walk with you in sideways wrath, and I will discipline you sevenfold according to your sins.
verses.26:29: And you will eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you will eat.
verses.26:30: And I will make your pillars desolate, and I will utterly destroy your wooden handmade objects, and I will place your corpses upon the corpses of your idols, and My soul will loathe you.
verses.26:31: And I will make your cities desolate, and I will lay waste your holy places, and I will by no means smell the aroma of your sacrifices.
verses.26:32: And I Myself will lay waste your land, and your enemies who dwell in it will be astonished at it.
verses.26:33: And I will scatter you among the nations, and the advancing sword will consume you; and your land will be desolate, and your cities will be desolate.
verses.26:34: Then the land will delight in its Sabbaths even all the days of its desolation,
verses.26:35: and you will be in the land of your enemies; then the land will keep Sabbath, and the land will delight in its Sabbaths. All the days of its desolation it will keep the Sabbaths that it did not keep during your Sabbaths, when you were dwelling in it.
verses.26:36: And as for those who are left of you, I will bring bondage into their heart in the land of their enemies, and the sound of a driven leaf will pursue them, and they will flee as those fleeing from war, and they will fall when no one is pursuing.
verses.26:37: And brother will disregard brother as in war, when no one is chasing, and you will not be able to stand against your enemies.
verses.26:38: And you will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
verses.26:39: And those who are left of you will decay because of your sins; in the land of their enemies they will melt away.
verses.26:40: And they will confess their sins and the sins of their fathers, that they transgressed and disregarded Me, and that they walked sideways against Me,
verses.26:41: and I walked with them in sideways wrath. And I will destroy them in the land of their enemies; then their uncircumcised heart will be put to shame, and then they will accept their sins.
verses.26:42: And I will remember the covenant of Jacob, and the covenant of Isaac and the covenant of Abraham I will remember, and the land I will remember.
verses.26:43: And the land will be forsaken by them; then the land will receive its Sabbaths when it is made desolate because of them, and they themselves will receive their own iniquities, because they disregarded My judgments and loathed My ordinances in their soul.
verses.26:44: And not even so, when they were in the land of their enemies, did I disregard them, nor did I loathe them so as to consume them, to break My covenant with them; for I am the Lord their God.
verses.26:45: And I will remember their former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, in the sight of the nations, to be their God; I am the Lord.
verses.26:46: These are My judgments and My ordinances, and the law which the Lord gave between Himself and the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
verses.27:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.27:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'Whoever makes a vow as a valuation of his life to the Lord,
verses.27:3: the valuation of a male from twenty years old to sixty years old shall be—his valuation shall be fifty didrachmas of silver by the holy weight.
verses.27:4: And the assessment of a female shall be thirty didrachmas.
verses.27:5: And if it is from five years old to twenty years, the valuation of a male shall be twenty didrachmas, and of a female, fourteen didrachmas.
verses.27:6: And from one month old to five years old, the valuation of a male shall be five didrachmas of silver, and of a female, three didrachmas.
verses.27:7: And if it is from sixty years old and above, if it is a male, the valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver, and if a female, ten didrachmas.
verses.27:8: And if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall assess him; just as the hand of the one who vowed is able, the priest shall assess him.
verses.27:9: Now if it is from the animals from which a gift is offered to the Lord, whoever gives from these to the Lord, it shall be holy.
verses.27:10: He shall not exchange it, good for bad, nor bad for good; and if he actually exchanges it, animal for animal, it and the substitute shall be holy.
verses.27:11: And if it is any unclean animal from which a gift is not offered to the Lord, he shall set the animal before the priest,
verses.27:12: and the priest shall assess it between good and bad; and according to whatever the priest assesses, so it shall stand.
verses.27:13: And if he actually redeems it, he shall add one-fifth to its valuation.
verses.27:14: And as for a person who consecrates his house as holy to the Lord, the priest shall assess it between good and bad; just as the priest assesses it, so it shall stand.
verses.27:15: And if the one who consecrated it redeems his house, he shall add to it one-fifth of the silver of the valuation, and it shall be his.
verses.27:16: Now if a person consecrates to the Lord part of the field of his possession, then the valuation shall be according to its seed: for a kor of barley, fifty didrachmas of silver.
verses.27:17: And if he consecrates his field from the year of release, it shall stand according to its valuation.
verses.27:18: And if he consecrates his field later, after the release, the priest shall calculate the silver for him for the remaining years until the year of release, and it shall be deducted from its assessment.
verses.27:19: And if the one who bought it redeems the field, he shall add one-fifth of the silver to its valuation, and it shall be his.
verses.27:20: And if he does not redeem the field, and he sells the field to another person, he shall never again redeem it;
verses.27:21: but the field, when the release has gone out, shall be holy to the Lord, like the land that has been set apart; it shall be a possession for the priest.
verses.27:22: And if he consecrates to the Lord part of the field that he has acquired, which is not part of the field of his possession,
verses.27:23: the priest shall calculate for him the total of the valuation from the year of release, and he shall pay the valuation on that day, holy to the Lord;
verses.27:24: and in the year of release, the field shall be returned to the person from whom he acquired it, to whom the possession of the land belonged.
verses.27:25: And every valuation shall be by holy weights; the didrachma shall be twenty obols.
verses.27:26: And every firstborn that is born among your animals shall belong to the Lord, and no one shall consecrate it, whether calf or sheep; it belongs to the Lord.
verses.27:27: And if it is of the unclean four-footed animals, he shall exchange it according to its valuation and add one-fifth to it, and it shall be his; and if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold according to its assessed value.
verses.27:28: But as for every devoted thing that a person devotes to the Lord from all that belongs to him, from human to animal and from a field of his possession, he shall not sell or redeem it; every devoted thing shall be most holy to the Lord.
verses.27:29: And everyone who is devoted from among human beings shall not be redeemed, but shall surely be put to death.
verses.27:30: Every tithe of the land, from the seed of the land and the fruit of the tree, belongs to the Lord; it is holy to the Lord.
verses.27:31: And if a person indeed redeems his tithe, he shall add one-fifth to it, and it shall be his.
verses.27:32: And every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything that comes in the counting under the rod, the tenth one shall be holy to the Lord.
verses.27:33: You shall not exchange good for bad; and if you actually exchange it, its substitute also shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'"
verses.27:34: These are the commandments that the Lord commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.

notes.1:1: Greek skenes tou martyriou ("tent of testimony") is the standard Septuagint rendering used throughout Leviticus where the Hebrew has "tent of meeting."
notes.1:4: Greek karpoma ("fire offering") is a cultic term for an offering consumed by fire on the altar; here and in 1:14 the Greek uses it where the Hebrew has "burnt offering."
notes.1:5: The Greek shifts to third-person plural verbs ("they shall slaughter," continuing in 1:6, 1:9, and 1:11-13) where the Hebrew uses singular verbs for the offerer's actions.
notes.1:10: Greek ton probaton ("the sheep") is used broadly in the Septuagint for small flock livestock, here explicitly encompassing both lambs and young goats (where the Hebrew reads "or").
notes.1:16: Greek syn tois pterois ("with the feathers") reflects an ancient interpretation of the rare Hebrew term often rendered "contents" or "plumage."
notes.2:1: Throughout chapter 2, the Greek uses thysia ("sacrifice") for what the Hebrew designates specifically as a grain offering (minchah), and here adds "It is a sacrifice" at the end of the verse.
notes.2:4: The Greek text literally reads ek libanou ("from frankincense"), an early copyist omission of kappa from ek klibanou ("from an oven," matching the Hebrew).
notes.2:7: Greek escharas ("hearth," or portable brazier/grate) stands where the Hebrew names a cooking pan, and the Greek omits the mention of "fine flour" found in the Hebrew.
notes.2:14: Greek chidra ("groats") denotes coarsely crushed, roasted unripe wheat grains; the translation preserves the Septuagint's stacked modifiers ("tender, fresh, roasted, crushed groats").
notes.3:1: Greek thysia soteriou ("sacrifice of deliverance," literally "of salvation/preservation") is the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew peace or well-being offering (shelamim).
notes.3:2: The Greek specifies plural "his hands" (also in 3:8 and 3:13, contrasting with singular "hand" in chapter 1 and the Hebrew) and explicitly names "the altar of the whole burnt offerings."
notes.3:9: The Greek reads "to God" rather than "to the Lord," and specifies "the unblemished loin" removed "along with the loin muscles" (psoai), where the Hebrew specifies the entire fat tail removed close to the backbone.
notes.3:14: The Greek text reads ep' autou ("upon it," referring to the altar at the end of 3:13), whereas some Greek manuscripts read ap' autou ("from it," matching the Hebrew).
notes.4:4: Greek 'skenes tou martyriou' ("tent of testimony") is the standard Septuagint rendering of Hebrew 'ohel moed' ("tent of meeting"), connecting the phrase with witness or testimony.
notes.4:5: The Greek adds "whose hands have been consecrated" (lit. "perfected in his hands"), a Septuagint idiom for priestly ordination not found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text of this verse.
notes.4:10: "Sacrifice of deliverance" translates Greek 'thysias tou soteriou' (lit. "sacrifice of salvation/deliverance"), the Septuagint term for the peace or well-being offering. The verb 'aphaireite' is second-person plural ("you remove"), likely an itacistic spelling of third-person singular passive 'aphaireitai' ("is removed").
notes.4:22: The Greek reads "the Lord their God" (plural 'auton'), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "his God" (singular).
notes.4:29: The Greek reads literally "the head of his sin/offense" ('tou hamartematos autou'), using the term for sin to designate the sin-offering animal, as 'hamartia' does throughout chapters 4-5.
notes.5:2: The Septuagint list differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text by naming "something unclean torn by wild beasts" ('therialotou akathartou') and "abominations" ('bdelygmaton', for swarming creatures), and by omitting the closing clause on hiddenness and guilt found in the Hebrew.
notes.5:4: The Greek reads "a lawless person" ('psyche he anomos') where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "if a person swears," and adds "before his eyes" ('pro ophthalmon').
notes.5:15: The Greek phrase "completely escapes a person" (lit. "escapes him with forgetfulness/oversight") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which speaks of committing a breach of faith.
notes.5:20: Verses 5:20-26 follow the Septuagint and Hebrew chapter division; most English Bibles number this section as Leviticus 6:1-7.
notes.5:24: The Greek "on the day he is convicted" ('he hemera elenchthe') differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "on the day of his guilt offering."
notes.6:2: Greek kausis literally means "burning" (corresponding to the hearth or firebed of the altar in the Hebrew text), and the Septuagint adds the closing clause "it shall not be extinguished," which is absent from the Masoretic Text.
notes.6:3: Greek katakarposis ("burnt residue") denotes the consumed remains of the burnt offering on the altar, where the Hebrew text refers to the fatty ashes.
notes.6:7: Throughout chapters 6-7, Greek thysia ("sacrifice") renders both the Hebrew grain offering (6:7-16; 7:9-10) and the animal sacrifice (7:11-37).
notes.6:14: Greek helikta ("rolled pieces") is a distinctive Septuagint rendering of an obscure Hebrew culinary term often interpreted as baked or folded pieces.
notes.6:20: The Greek clause literally places a personal pronoun ("whoever is sprinkled on it") as the subject of the passive verb "shall be washed" (plyno), a verb normally used for washing garments, reflecting a compressed translation of the Hebrew syntax.
notes.7:3: Greek ten osphyn ("the loin") appears here where the Masoretic Text specifies the animal's fat tail.
notes.7:11: Greek thysia soteriou ("sacrifice of deliverance") renders the Hebrew peace or fellowship offering throughout Leviticus.
notes.7:15: Unlike the Masoretic Text, the Septuagint includes auto estai ("shall belong to him"), assigning the flesh of the deliverance sacrifice of praise to the officiating priest.
notes.7:30: The Septuagint adds "and the lobe of the liver" (absent from the Masoretic Text) and renders the Hebrew "wave offering" as a "placed" gift (epithenai doma, corresponding to epithema in 7:34; similarly brachion, "shoulder/arm," in 7:32-34 corresponds to Hebrew "thigh").
notes.7:33: The Greek text reads neuter to ("that which is from the sons of Aaron"), whereas other Greek witnesses and the Masoretic Text read masculine ("the one from among the sons of Aaron").
notes.8:7: The Septuagint reads plural αὐτούς ("them") for the tunic and sash before switching to singular αὐτόν ("him") for the robe and shoulder-piece, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text uses the singular throughout.
notes.8:8: The Greek renders the Hebrew priestly vestments as ἐπωμίς ("shoulder-piece," for ephod), λόγιον ("oracle," for breastpiece), and τὴν δήλωσιν καὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ("the manifestation and the truth," for Urim and Thummim).
notes.8:11: In the Septuagint order, the anointing of the tent and its contents follows the sprinkling and anointing of the altar and basin at the end of verse 11 rather than appearing in verse 10 as in the Hebrew text.
notes.8:18: In this Greek text, verse 18 incorporates the material traditionally numbered as verse 19 ("And Moses slaughtered the ram, and Moses poured the blood upon the altar all around").
notes.8:30: The source Greek text overlaps between verses 29 and 30, duplicates the final phrase ("and the garments of his sons with him") in verse 30, and reads προσέῤῥνεν (a spelling of προσέρρανεν, "sprinkled"); like the Septuagint generally, it omits the closing sanctification clause found in the Hebrew text.
notes.9:4: Greek θυσία σωτηρίου ("sacrifice of deliverance") is the characteristic Septuagint rendering for the Hebrew peace or fellowship offering.
notes.9:7: The Septuagint reads "and your house" (τοῦ οἴκου σου) rather than the Hebrew "and for the people," and includes "to Moses" (τῷ Μωυσῇ) at the end of the verse.
notes.9:20: The Greek reverses the verb numbers of the Hebrew text, reading singular ἐπέθηκεν ("he placed") followed by plural ἀνήνεγκαν ("they offered up").
notes.9:24: Greek ἐξέστη ("were amazed" or "were astonished") expresses a Septuagint reaction of awe rather than the Hebrew "shouted for joy."
notes.10:3: 'Deeply stricken' translates Greek κατενύχθη ('pierced/stunned with grief'), where the Hebrew MT reads 'kept silent'; likewise 'in the whole congregation' renders ἐν πάσῃ συναγωγῇ (MT: 'before all the people').
notes.10:4: The Greek text reads Μισαδαὶ ('Misadai') and Ἀζιήλ ('Aziel'), where the Hebrew MT has Mishael and Uzziel.
notes.10:6: 'Remove the turban from your head' translates the rare Greek verb ἀποκιδαρώσετε (literally 'un-turban', from κίδαρις, the priestly turban), whereas the Hebrew MT refers to leaving the hair unbound.
notes.10:14: The Septuagint terms ἀφόρισμα ('separated offering'), ἀφαίρεμα ('contribution'), βραχίων ('shoulder'), and θυσίαι τοῦ σωτηρίου ('sacrifices of deliverance') correspond to the Hebrew MT's wave offering, heave offering, thigh, and peace offerings; the Greek also reads 'in a holy place' and 'your household' (MT: 'in a clean place' and 'your daughters').
notes.10:18: The Greek joins κατὰ πρόσωπον ἔσω ('right inside') to the command to eat the offering and concludes 'just as the Lord commanded me' (Hebrew MT: 'just as I commanded').
notes.11:5: The Greek text reverses the order of the Hebrew MT in vv. 5-6, listing δασύποδα ('hare') in v. 5 and χοιρογρύλλιον ('rock badger') in v. 6 (MT: rock badger in v. 5, hare in v. 6).
notes.11:14: Verse 11:15 (listing the raven in the Hebrew MT) is absent from this Greek text, while γλαῦκα ('owl') appears twice in the bird list (vv. 16 and 19).
notes.11:22: The four edible insects in Greek are βροῦχον ('wingless locust'), ἀττάκην ('attakes', an unidentified kind of locust), ἀκρίδα ('locust'), and ὀφιομάχην (literally 'snake-fighter', a kind of locust or grasshopper).
notes.11:26: The Greek text omits the negation before 'splits hoof-clefts' (ὀνυχιστῆρας ὀνυχίζει), whereas the Hebrew MT reads 'is not cloven-footed.'
notes.11:47: 'Those that bring forth alive what is eaten' literally translates Greek τῶν ζωογονούντων τὰ ἐσθιόμενα (taking the neuter plural as the direct object of ζωογονέω), whereas the Hebrew MT reads 'the living creature that may be eaten.'
notes.12:2: Greek σπερματισθῇ (aorist passive of σπερματίζω) literally means "is seeded" or "receives seed," denoting conception.
notes.12:3: Greek uses the active verb περιτεμεῖ ("shall circumcise") with no new explicit subject, continuing the mother from v. 2 as grammatical subject (or acting impersonally as "one shall circumcise"), whereas the Hebrew text is passive.
notes.12:4: Greek reads ἐν αἵματι ἀκαθάρτῳ αὐτῆς ("in her unclean blood," also in v. 5) where the Hebrew has "blood of purification," and reads ἀγγίου ("vessel") where other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew read ἁγίου ("holy thing").
notes.12:7: Greek makes the priest the explicit active subject of καθαριεῖ αὐτήν ("he shall cleanse her"), whereas the Hebrew text reads "and she shall be clean."
notes.12:8: "Her hand does not find what is sufficient" preserves a literal Greek rendering of a Semitic idiom meaning she cannot afford a lamb.
notes.13:2: Greek "a bright scar of a mark" forms a single phrase rather than the three alternatives ("swelling, eruption, or bright spot") of the Hebrew text. Throughout this chapter, Greek "leprosy" (lepra) covers a range of scaly or discoloring skin conditions rather than solely modern Hansen's disease.
notes.13:4: The Greek text uses the feminine pronoun ("its" or "her") for "its flesh" and "its skin" (matching the feminine gender of "bright spot" or "affliction") and includes the clause "and it is dim," which is absent from the Masoretic Hebrew here.
notes.13:11: The Greek text reads positively "and isolate him," whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "he shall not shut him up."
notes.13:15: The Greek renders the Hebrew for "raw/living flesh" as "healthy flesh" (also in vv. 10, 16) and takes "the healthy flesh" as the subject of "defile," where the Masoretic Hebrew divides the clauses with the priest as subject.
notes.13:27: Although vv. 24-28 concern burns, the Greek text includes the clause "it has broken out in the sore" (echoing v. 22), which is absent from the Masoretic Hebrew here.
notes.13:31: The Greek text reads "of the wound" (traumatos) in the first clause before "of the scab" (thrausmatos) in the second, and reads "yellowish hair" where the Masoretic Hebrew has "black hair."
notes.13:39: Greek alphos refers to a benign dull-white skin rash; the Greek text also uses the future tense "it will break out" and repeats "he is clean."
notes.13:45: The Greek text reads "loosened" (not "torn"), "head uncovered" (not "hair disheveled"), "around his mouth" (not "upper lip"), and passive "he shall be called unclean" where the Masoretic Hebrew reads active "he shall cry out, 'Unclean, unclean!'"
notes.13:55: The Greek text reads "it is firmly set in the garment or in the warp or in the weft," diverging from the Masoretic Hebrew ("it is a corrosion, whether on the back or on the front of it").
notes.14:14: Greek ἄκρον literally means "extremity" or "tip" (here and in vv. 17, 25, 28), reflecting the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew term for the thumb and big toe.
notes.14:19: The Greek text reads τοῦ ἀκαθάρτου ("the unclean one") and ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ ("from his sin"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "from his uncleanness."
notes.14:39: This Greek text reads οὐ διεχύθη ("has not spread," as in Codex Vaticanus), in contrast to other Septuagint witnesses and the Hebrew text ("has spread").
notes.14:40: This Greek text reads τοὺς λίθους· ἔστιν ἡ ἁφή· ("the stones; there is the plague;"), omitting the relative pronoun ἐν οἷς ("in which") found in other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew text.
notes.14:42: This Greek text reads λίθους ἀπεξυσμένους στερεούς ("scraped solid stones," as in Codex Vaticanus), whereas other Septuagint witnesses read "other scraped stones" and the Hebrew text reads "other stones."
notes.15:3: The Greek uses medical terminology (gonos, "semen/genital fluid," the root of gonorrhues, "the one with a discharge," used throughout the chapter) and synesteken ("is obstructed/congealed"). Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Septuagint omits "or" between the two conditions and adds the closing clause "all the days of the discharge of his body... it is his uncleanness."
notes.15:9: The Septuagint specifies "saddle of a donkey" (episagma onou) and adds "until evening" (heos hesperas), both absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.15:23: The Greek syntax is notably difficult: the feminine participle ouses ("while she is") and feminine pronoun autes ("her") refer to the woman rather than to an object on the bed or seat as in the Hebrew, while the Codex Vaticanus text concludes with the neuter akatharton ("it shall be unclean").
notes.15:31: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text commands Moses and Aaron to "separate" the Israelites from their uncleanness, the Septuagint renders the verb as eulabeis poiesete ("make cautious" or "circumspect").
notes.16:1: The Septuagint explicitly adds "strange fire" (pyr allotrion, echoing Lev 10:1), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads only "when they drew near before the Lord."
notes.16:8: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Azazel," the Septuagint translates with to apopompaio ("the one to be sent away," i.e., the scapegoat; cf. apopompe, "sending away," in 16:10 and eis aphesin, "for release," in 16:26).
notes.16:24: As in 16:20 ("make cleansing for the priests"), the Septuagint expands the atonement formula here by adding "and for his household" and "as for the priests" (hos peri ton hiereon).
notes.16:29: Following the Codex Vaticanus tradition, the Greek text omits "on the tenth day of the month" after "in the seventh month" and uses an aorist imperative ("humble your souls") rather than a future verb; it also renders the resident alien as proselutos ho proskeimenos ("the proselyte who is joined").
notes.16:34: The Septuagint renders the closing verb as future passive poiethesetai ("Once a year it shall be done"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a narrative past tense ("And he did as the Lord commanded Moses").
notes.17:4: The Septuagint includes an expanded doublet naming the burnt offering and deliverance offering (σωτήριον, corresponding to the Hebrew peace/fellowship offering) and renders the sanctuary as the 'tent of testimony' (σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου) rather than 'tent of meeting'.
notes.17:7: Greek τοῖς ματαίοις ('the worthless things', a standard Septuagint expression for idols) corresponds to 'goat-demons' in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:8: The Septuagint reads 'the sons of the resident aliens' (τῶν υἱῶν τῶν προσηλύτων), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads simply 'the sojourners'.
notes.17:11: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'is in the blood' and 'by the life', the Septuagint equates the life (ψυχή, 'life/soul') directly with 'its blood' and states that its blood makes atonement 'in place of' (ἀντί) the life.
notes.18:3: The Septuagint uses the passive οὐ ποιηθήσεται ('it shall not be done') in the first clause before shifting to the active οὐ ποιήσετε ('you shall not do so') in the second.
notes.18:6: Greek ἀσχημοσύνη (literally 'unseemliness' or 'shameful nakedness') is used throughout this chapter as the Septuagint euphemism for nakedness in the idiom 'uncover nakedness'.
notes.18:21: Greek λατρεύειν ἄρχοντι ('to serve a ruler') corresponds to the Hebrew phrase commonly translated 'to pass through [the fire] to Molech', and τὸ ὄνομα τὸ ἅγιον reads 'the holy name' rather than 'the name of your God'.
notes.18:25: Greek προσώχθισεν ('became disgusted with', also in v. 28) replaces the physical metaphor of the Hebrew Masoretic Text ('vomited out').
notes.18:28: The Septuagint reads the plural 'the nations' (τοῖς ἔθνεσιν), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the singular 'the nation'.
notes.19:5: The Greek text reads δεκάτην ("tithe" or "tenth"), a notable Septuagint manuscript reading where other witnesses have δεκτὴν ("acceptable," matching the Hebrew).
notes.19:23: The Greek adds the clause "which the Lord God is giving you" and uses purification language ("cleanse away its uncleanness," "uncleansed") rather than the Hebrew's circumcision imagery.
notes.19:26: The Greek reads "upon the mountains" (ἐπὶ τῶν ὀρέων), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants than the Masoretic Text's "with the blood."
notes.19:29: Following Hebrew negative coordination literally, the Greek does not repeat the negative before "and the land shall be filled with lawlessness," though the negation extends to both clauses.
notes.19:36: A chous (χοῦς) is a Greek liquid measure of roughly three liters; the Greek lists three measuring standards where the Hebrew lists four.
notes.20:2: Here and in verses 3-5, the Greek translates the Hebrew as "a ruler" (ἄρχοντι) or "the rulers" (τοὺς ἄρχοντας), reading it from the root for "king/ruler" rather than as the proper name Molech.
notes.20:3: The Greek reads "the name of those consecrated to Me" (τῶν ἡγιασμένων μοι), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "My holy name."
notes.20:9: Here and in verses 11-13, 16, and 27, the Greek renders the Hebrew idiom "his/their blood is upon him/them" as "guilty" (ἔνοχος/ἔνοχοι).
notes.20:20: The Greek twice reads "his female relative" (τῆς συγγενοῦς αὐτοῦ) and omits "they shall bear their sin," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's references to an uncle's wife and uncle.
notes.20:22: The Greek reads "be disgusted with" (προσοχθίσῃ) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "vomit you out."
